concept.name: dsp_ab_lab_measure_simulate_listen_2026_08_02
concept.aliases: "is the DSP making it sound bad", "measure audio instead of arguing", "A/B test the enhancer", "simulate AudioStream chain offline", "why do I need 70-80% volume", "whisper too quiet", "level-matched listening test", "dsp-ab-lab", "FastTanh vs softsign", "yt-dlp SABR workaround"
concept.symptoms: Suspicion that the browser's audio DSP is coloring/harming the sound, or that it fails to make quiet content audible — with only subjective impressions to go on.
concept.when_to_recall: Before ANY retune of the AudioStream enhancer constants; whenever audio quality is disputed; when designing the quiet-lifter; when a future model wants to "improve" the audio chain based on vibes.
concept.wrong_instinct: Arguing from theory or tweaking constants by ear alone. Also: comparing processed vs raw WITHOUT level-matching — the processed version is ~4 dB hotter and louder ALWAYS sounds "better"; the level-matched clip (C) is the only honest tonal comparison. Also: using softsign x/(1+|x|) as "FastTanh" in simulations — the shipped code is the Pade (3,2) rational: w*(27+w^2)/(27+9w^2), clamped at |w|=3 where it equals exactly 1.0.
concept.human_rationale:
LAYMAN: when people disagree about sound, the answer is not a louder opinion — it is three short clips: the song untouched (A), the song through the browser's enhancement exactly as shipped (B), and the enhanced version turned down to match the untouched loudness (C). Played through the same speakers on a clean path, your ears become a measuring instrument. On 2026-08-02 this protocol acquitted the browser's enhancer: no metal, no buzz, a touch of warmth — and proved its LIMIT: it barely helps whispered voices, because it boosts bass and treble while a whisper's intelligibility lives in the middle frequencies it leaves alone.
DEVELOPER — THE METHOD (tool: gorilla-firefox-toolkit/modules/dsp-ab-lab.py): 1. FETCH the disputed content itself (not a synthetic sweep): yt-dlp --extractor-args "youtube:player_client=android" -x --audio-format wav URL (2026-08 reality: default clients are SABR-blocked; android client passes.) 2. MEASURE: ffmpeg loudnorm (EBU R128) for integrated LUFS + LRA; 400ms-window RMS percentiles to LOCATE the whispers (p25 floor) and the loud passages (p90); band-split the whisper passages USING THE CHAIN'S OWN one-pole math at ITS OWN corners (220/3500 Hz) to see which band the problem lives in. 3. SIMULATE the chain bit-exact (constants in the tool's SYNC BLOCK mirror dom/media/AudioStream.cpp — keep them in sync or the lab lies): bass=LP220(x); treble=x-LP3500(x); mid=x-bass-treble # perfect reconstruction eb=1.8*bass; eb+=0.2*FastTanh(0.4*eb); et=1.4*treble y=(eb+mid+et)*1.1 out = y if |y|<=0.9 else sign(y)*(0.9+0.1*FastTanh(10*(|y|-0.9))) 4. LISTEN, level-matched: build testA_raw / testB_dsp / testC_dsp_levelmatched from the auto-found whisper+loud segments; play A->B->C with 8s gaps via pw-play on a clean 44.1-native path, browser paused. Three questions only: metallic/vibration in B that A lacks? C vs A at equal loudness — warmer or dirtier? whispers more INTELLIGIBLE or just bassier?
concept.execution_logic: MEASURED RESULTS — G1 test ballad (the retired G1 brand traced to this clip), 2026-08-02: source: -15.0 LUFS integrated, true peak 0.0 dBTP, LRA 13.7 LU (double-normal dynamics); whispers -27.9 dBFS RMS; whisper energy: bass 49% / mid 49% / treble 2%. Shipped chain delivers: whispers +4.4 dB, loud +3.9 dB (near-flat = fixed tone control, NOT a loudness intelligence); per-band on whispers: bass +6.6 dB, MID +0.8 dB, treble +3.8 dB (nothing up there to boost). Limiter engagement 0.138% (asleep). LISTENING VERDICT (owner, 3 runs, silent system, sink@44100): B and C "sounded good", differences "minor/minute", no metal, no vibration -> chain EXONERATED for harshness; benefit real but subtle. Consistent with the numbers. WHY THE 70-80% VOLUME CRANK EXISTS: whisper leaves the browser at ~-23.5 dBFS; the missing ~20 dB comes from sliders + the kernel EAPD +5.5 dB. Working as designed; the design was never going to solve a 13.7-LU ballad. THE FIX STILL TO BUILD — envelope-tracked quiet-lifter (G1's GOAL was right, its memoryless waveshaper math was the disaster; do it properly): - envelope follower on post-volume signal (attack ~5-10ms, release ~250-400ms); - upward gain curve: up to +10..12 dB when envelope below ~-30 dBFS, unity by ~-18 dBFS, smooth (e.g. half-cosine) interpolation between — gain follows the ENVELOPE, never the instantaneous sample (that distinction is the entire anti-distortion lesson); - placement: in AudioStream after software volScale, before the enhancer; existing 0.9 FastTanh knee remains the final safety; - validate with THIS lab first (simulate on the ballad, demand: whispers +8..12 dB, loud +0..1 dB, limiter engagement still <1%), then level-matched listen, then patch. Related evidence: SECOND.BRAIN/Chroma.DB.and.Brain.xml/AUDIO.AUDIT.2026-08-02/.
concept.verified: 2026-08-02 (measurements + owner listening test; tool committed to toolkit)
